meta.name: Dehydration — Difficult IV Access in a Fragile Nursing Home Resident

patient.name: Walter Osei
patient.chiefComplaint: Poor oral intake and weakness for three days

history.hpi: Nursing home staff report the patient has eaten and drunk very little over the past three days, becoming progressively weaker and less interactive. No fever reported by staff. He is oriented to person only at baseline per staff, unchanged today.
history.lastOralIntake: A few sips of water this morning per staff
history.events: Nursing staff noted decreased intake over three days and called EMS after he was found difficult to arouse for breakfast

scene.dispatch: 71-year-old male, nursing home, weak and not acting right
scene.location: Skilled nursing facility, resident room, patient in bed
scene.bystanders: Charge nurse present with medication administration record
visualCues: Patient thin, frail-appearing, lying in bed
Dry, cracked lips and dry oral mucosa
Thin, fragile-appearing veins visible on both forearms and hands

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew finds a frail 71-year-old male in bed, arousable but slow to respond, with dry mucous membranes and tenting skin consistent with volume depletion after several days of poor intake.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, weak; skin tenting present
otherFindings: Dry, cracked lips and dry oral mucosa
Slow to answer questions, oriented to person only (baseline per staff)
Thin, fragile veins on both forearms and hands
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I'm just... tired. Haven't felt like eating."

transitions.if: IV access obtained within two attempts
transitions.condition: Crew recognizes signs of hypovolemia, checks blood glucose, and successfully establishes peripheral IV access within two attempts and under 90 seconds despite fragile veins.

transitions.if: IV access fails twice / exceeds 90 seconds
transitions.condition: Crew attempts IV access on the fragile veins but fails after two attempts or exceeds 90 seconds, meeting criteria to place an IO needle instead.

phases.name: IV access obtained within two attempts
phases.description: Crew successfully cannulates a peripheral vein despite the patient's thin, fragile veins, checks blood glucose, and initiates an isotonic fluid bolus.
phases.triggerCondition: After recognizing signs of hypovolemia (tachycardia, hypotension, dry mucous membranes, skin tenting), the crew successfully establishes peripheral IV access on the first or second attempt within 90 seconds.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, IV infusing without infiltration
otherFindings: 22-gauge IV in place, patent, no infiltration

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize hypovolemia from dry mucous membranes, tenting skin, tachycardia, borderline BP
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Signs of poor perfusion (due to a medical cause) such as one or more of the following: Tachycardia or bradycardia for age... Mucous membrane hydration... Skin (turgor, rash)
expectedActions.rationale: Recognizing volume depletion drives the decision to obtain IV access and give fluids.

expectedActions.shortAction: Check blood glucose to rule out hypoglycemia as a contributing cause
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Check blood sugar, and correct if less than 60 mg/dL
expectedActions.rationale: Altered baseline mentation and poor intake could reflect hypoglycemia, which must be excluded.

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish peripheral IV access, using a proximal/larger vein given fragile skin and small distal veins
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Establish IV access. If unable to obtain within two attempts or less than 90 seconds, place an IO needle
expectedActions.rationale: Reliable IV access is required to deliver fluid resuscitation in a hypovolemic patient.

expectedActions.shortAction: Administer 500 mL NS bolus IV, pressure-infused over less than 15 minutes, reassess
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: IV fluid volume goal attained by giving boluses that are pressure infused over less than 15 minutes each... Fluid goal of up to 30 mL/kg of isotonic fluid by administering rapid, predetermined boluses (e.g., 500 mL) unless the MAP goal is achieved, or pulmonary edema develops
expectedActions.rationale: A predetermined 500 mL bolus, reassessed against a MAP goal, is the protocol's standard approach to hypovolemia; up to 30 mL/kg (about 2,250 mL for this patient) may be given.

transitions.condition: After the fluid bolus, heart rate and blood pressure trend toward normal and mentation improves toward baseline.

phases.name: IV access fails twice / exceeds 90 seconds
phases.description: Peripheral IV attempts fail on the patient's thin, fragile, rolling veins. Per protocol, the crew transitions to IO access to avoid further delay in fluid resuscitation.
phases.triggerCondition: Two peripheral IV attempts fail, or 90 seconds elapse without successful cannulation, on the fragile veins.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, weak; two failed IV attempt sites with minor bruising
otherFindings: Two failed peripheral IV attempts, small hematomas at attempt sites
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Ow... can you please stop poking me?"

expectedActions.shortAction: Place IO needle after two failed IV attempts / 90 seconds elapsed
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Establish IV access. If unable to obtain within two attempts or less than 90 seconds, place an IO needle
expectedActions.rationale: Protocol mandates prompt escalation to IO to avoid delaying fluid resuscitation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Administer 500 mL NS bolus via IO, pressure-infused, reassess
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: IV fluid volume goal attained by giving boluses that are pressure infused over less than 15 minutes each... Fluid goal of up to 30 mL/kg of isotonic fluid by administering rapid, predetermined boluses (e.g., 500 mL) unless the MAP goal is achieved, or pulmonary edema develops
expectedActions.rationale: Fluid resuscitation proceeds via IO exactly as it would via IV once access is secured.

transitions.condition: After the IO fluid bolus, heart rate and blood pressure trend toward normal and mentation improves toward baseline.

phases.name: Fluid bolus given and improving
phases.description: Patient's perfusion improves following isotonic fluid resuscitation. Crew continues reassessment en route to the hospital.
phases.triggerCondition: Following a 500 mL isotonic fluid bolus (via IV or IO), the patient's heart rate and blood pressure trend toward normal and mentation improves.

otherFindings: More conversant, oriented to person and place
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel a little more like myself."

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vital signs and mental status; continue fluids toward MAP goal of 65 mmHg
expectedActions.rationale: Ongoing reassessment against the MAP target guides whether further fluid boluses are needed en route.

expectedActions.shortAction: Provide advance notification to the receiving hospital
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Provide advanced notification to the hospital
expectedActions.rationale: Advance notice allows the receiving facility to prepare for a dehydrated, hemodynamically improving patient.
